title: Matcap Material Gallery with Real-Time Swapping
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive Matcap Material Gallery with real-time material swapping, undo/redo history, and multi-modal controls.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e).
- Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 0, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- The scene contains a gallery of 5 geometry pedestals arranged in a horizontal row (x positions: -4, -2, 0, 2, 4; y=0; z=0).
- Each pedestal is a CylinderGeometry(0.4, 0.4, 0.15, 32) at y=-0.8 with a MeshStandardMaterial colored 0x333344.
- On top of each pedestal, place a showcase object:
  - Pedestal 0: SphereGeometry(0.6, 64, 64)
  - Pedestal 1: BoxGeometry(0.9, 0.9, 0.9)
  - Pedestal 2: TorusKnotGeometry(0.4, 0.15, 128, 32)
  - Pedestal 3: TorusGeometry(0.45, 0.2, 32, 64)
  - Pedestal 4: IcosahedronGeometry(0.6, 2)
- Each showcase object sits at y=0.2 on its pedestal.
- Add one AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.3) and one DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 0.7) at position (5, 10, 5).

## Matcap Materials
- Generate 6 procedural matcap textures using Canvas2D (each 256x256). Each matcap is a radial gradient sphere simulation:
  - Matcap 0 'Ruby': center #ff4444, mid #aa1111, edge #330000
  - Matcap 1 'Gold': center #ffee88, mid #cc9900, edge #443300
  - Matcap 2 'Ice': center #aaeeff, mid #4488cc, edge #112244
  - Matcap 3 'Jade': center #66ffaa, mid #228855, edge #003322
  - Matcap 4 'Chrome': center #ffffff, mid #888888, edge #111111
  - Matcap 5 'Obsidian': center #444466, mid #222233, edge #000000
- Create each as a THREE.CanvasTexture and use THREE.MeshMatcapMaterial for each showcase object.
- Initially assign matcap index 0 to object 0, index 1 to object 1, etc. (object 4 gets matcap 4).

## Selection & Interaction
- Maintain a selectedIndex (0-4) indicating which showcase object is selected. Default: 0.
- The selected object should have a visible highlight: a wireframe outline (clone geometry, slightly scaled up by 1.08, wireframe material colored 0x00ffff, linewidth 1).
- Clicking on a showcase object (via raycasting) selects it.
- Keyboard Left/Right arrows cycle selectedIndex (wrap around 0-4).
- Keyboard Up/Down arrows cycle the matcap material on the selected object through the 6 matcaps (wrap around 0-5). Up increments matcap index, Down decrements.
- Keyboard 'R' triggers a slow rotation animation toggle on the selected object (rotates around Y at 0.02 rad/frame when active, stops when toggled off).

## DOM UI
- A top-left HUD panel (id='hud-panel') with dark semi-transparent background showing:
  - Current selected object index and geometry name (id='hud-selected')
  - Current matcap name applied to selected object (id='hud-matcap')
  - Rotation status of selected object (id='hud-rotation')
  - Total material swaps counter (id='hud-swaps')
- A bottom-center button bar with:
  - 6 matcap swatch buttons (id='swatch-0' through 'swatch-5'), each 40x40px colored with the matcap center color. Clicking a swatch applies that matcap to the selected object.
  - An 'Undo' button (id='btn-undo') and 'Redo' button (id='btn-redo').
- Keyboard 'Z' triggers undo, keyboard 'Y' triggers redo.

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain a history stack of material assignment states. Each entry is an array of 5 matcap indices (one per object).
- Push a new snapshot onto the history whenever any matcap assignment changes.
- Undo restores the previous snapshot; redo re-applies the next snapshot.
- History pointer tracks current position. New changes after undo discard future entries.
- Maximum history depth: 50 entries.

## Comparison Mode
- Pressing 'C' toggles comparison mode. In comparison mode:
  - All 5 objects get the SAME matcap as the currently selected object's matcap.
  - A label (id='comparison-label') appears saying 'COMPARISON MODE'.
  - Pressing 'C' again restores each object to its matcap from before comparison mode was entered.
  - Entering comparison mode does NOT push to undo history. Exiting restores original state.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - selectedIndex: number (0-4)
  - matcapAssignments: array of 5 numbers (matcap index per object, 0-5)
  - matcapNames: array of 6 strings ['Ruby','Gold','Ice','Jade','Chrome','Obsidian']
  - objectNames: array of 5 strings ['Sphere','Box','TorusKnot','Torus','Icosahedron']
  - rotationStates: array of 5 booleans (whether each object is rotating)
  - objectRotationsY: array of 5 numbers (current Y rotation of each object)
  - totalSwaps: number
  - historyLength: number (total entries in history stack)
  - historyPointer: number (current position in history, 0-based)
  - comparisonMode: boolean
  - comparisonSavedAssignments: array of 5 numbers or null
  - selectedObjectWorldPos: {x, y, z} world position of selected object
  - cameraPosition: {x, y, z}
  - showcaseObjectCount: number (should be 5)
  - matcapCount: number (should be 6)
  - wireframeVisible: boolean (whether highlight wireframe is visible)
  - frameCount: number (incremented each frame)

## Animation
- Run a standard requestAnimationFrame loop. Each frame:
  - Update rotations for objects with rotation enabled.
  - Update all __3D_STATE__ fields.
  - Render the scene.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation. Material assignments must be consistent integers 0-5. Undo/redo must perfectly restore matcap assignment arrays. Comparison mode must be reversible without data loss. Rotation values must be finite and NaN-free.
